newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul won slides to end lower despite BOK support.
newsitem.headline: Seoul won slides to end lower despite BOK support.

text.p: The South Korean won ended Friday's trading a little lower against the U.S. unit, despite earlier dollar sales by the central Bank of Korea, dealers said.
But banks shied away from breaking the 885 mark, which is seen as being strongly guarded by the central bank, they said.
The central bank sold dollars at 884.40 won during early morning trading, traders said. The bank has refused to comment on talk of its intervention in interbank trading.
The won ended the day at 884.90, compared to Thursday's close of 884.00. It opened Friday at 884.70.
"The dollar has already risen by 20 won since the beginning of the month and it still has some momentum left," said a local bank dealer. "Everyone feels that the 885 level will be broken next week."
A steady inflow of import settlements, reflecting the nation's widening trade deficit, and the dollar's strength on world markets remains a strong drag on the local currency.

Fears that overseas creditors will tighten funds to Korean banks following the corporate collapse of the Hanbo and Sammi groups, leading to an even shorter supply of dollars, was also a dark cloud on trading.
